newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks failed to maintain early rises on Monday as consolidation outpaced buying interest shown in primary blue chips, brokers said.
They said rising outstanding margin loans versus customer deposits at brokerage houses also pressured investor sentiment.
Debt defaults by two listed firms over the weekend sent investors scurrying away from smaller-capitalised companies with high debt-to-equity ratios.
The composite stock index lost 1.49 points to 745.40, off the day's high of 753.56. The sub-index for small-capitalised shares shed 4.48 points to 1,931.86.

"Except a handful of blue chips, the market in general remained weak," said Park Doo-hyun at Hyundai Securities. "I expect another rally in the second half but the market needs to consolidate further before it."
Brokers said onshore funds and improved macro-economic indicators released over the weekend also contributed to rising blue chips.

The May industrial output grew 6.1 percent on the year from a 10.0 percent rise a year earlier. Inventory growth was the lowest in 20 months at 11.7 percent. The defaults on debt ratio fell to 0.23 percent in May from 0.25 percent in April.
Samsung Electronics rose 500 won to 70,500 and LG Electronics gained 700 won to 16,500 with heavy trading volume of 456,530 shares.
Hopes for future growth prospects boosted LG Information and Communications by 2,000 won to 110,000.
But foreign selling pushed heavily-index weighted KEPCO to close at 26,500, down 400 won, which brokers blamed for a part of the main index decline.
Loan defaults by Tae Sung Machinery and Construction, and Keum Kang Leather Co hit smaller companies hard, brokers said.

Tongkook Corp went limit down, shedding 340 won to 3,960. Both Tongkook Spinning Co and Tongkook General Electronics also fell to their lower limits of 5,220 and 7,820 respectively, down 450 won and 680.

The Korea Stock Exchange suspended Hwan Yung Industry Co share trading during the afternoon session after a court ordered the reinforcing bar producer to begin liquidation. It stood at 2,000 before the trading suspension, far below its par value of 5,000 won.
Park Key-pyong of Hanyang Securities said the market would move in a boxed range of 750-730 for the time being.
